items.title: USN-9130-1: zutils vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that zcat in zutils incorrectly handled the -v option, leading to a buffer overflow. If a user were tricked into opening a specially crafted compressed file, an attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service or execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9129-1: ZBar vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that ZBar incorrectly handled certain QR codes, leading to a heap-based buffer overflow. If a user or automated system were tricked into scanning a specially crafted QR code, an attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information or execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9128-1: YADIFA vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that YADIFA did not check for infinite pointer loops when parsing DNS packets. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause YADIFA to consume excessive CPU resources, leading to a denial of service.

items.title: USN-9127-1: Syntastic vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Syntastic searched the current directory and its parents for checker configuration files. items.title: USN-9126-1: tmpreaper vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that tmpreaper incorrectly handled certain mount operations, leading to a race condition. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to create arbitrary files, leading to privilege escalation.

items.title: USN-9124-1: RenderDoc vulnerabilities
items.summary: It was discovered that RenderDoc did not properly verify array sizes when serialising strings, leading to an integer overflow. items.title: USN-9123-1: mechanize vulnerability
items.summary: Erik Krogh Kristensen and Rasmus Petersen discovered that mechanize used an inefficient regular expression to parse authentication headers. A malicious server could possibly use this issue to cause mechanize to consume excessive resources, leading to a denial of service.
